faces.f: To the soldier, war is famine; to the scavenger, a feast.
Innistrad is a place where dreams invade the mind and mere shadows exact a terrible toll.
It took three years for it to occur to him to use the chain as a weapon, but once it did, he made up for lost time.
"The undead are not 'awakened.' They are evicted when there is no room left in the pit for more bodies."
"Wisdom from the past is best gathered directly from the source."

"A basilisk's gaze is effective, but disposing of physical remains is a tiresome task. It's far more discreet to dissolve one's victim entirely."
—Szadek
All crave the Blessed Sleep. Few receive it.
"I admit, I am a creature of the city. The sights, the nightly excitement, the abundance of fine drink . . ."
As they fought the Eldrazi, many vampires learned to live among humans. Others were unable to make the adjustment.
If there's anything a werewolf hates, it's a collar—especially Avacyn's Collar, the symbol of her church.
The shaman rattles not to inspire a battle fury but to drown out the shrieks of those fleeing the Eldrazi.
Heavy light flooded across the landscape, cloaking everything in deep crimson.
Chandra never believed in using her "inside voice."
Goblins journey to the sacrificial peaks in pairs so that the rare survivor might be able to relate the details of the other's grisly demise.
Nothing evens the odds like a little lightning.
A goblin raid is a delicate gambit—a blend of stealth, precision, and screaming death.
"I've been all over this world. I even remember some of those places."

"Behind every devil's mayhem lurks a demon's scheme."
—Rem Karolus, Blade of the Inquisitors
The larger the crowd, the harder it is for them to run away.
Some Akroans make the dangerous pilgrimage to the volcanic temples of Purphoros, where oracles known as flamespeakers glean omens from lava.
They'll attack whatever's in front of them—as long as you tell them where that is.
It came as a cruel answer to the farmers' prayers.
The oil sloshes against his skull as he nears his destination: the Frogtosser Games and the lighting of the Flaming Boggart.

"Who'd want to ignite things one at a time?"
—Chandra Nalaar

"The maaka remain loyal to us in this time of strife. We don't even have to feed them—our enemies do."
—Nedja, Gruul shaman
Each small blaze she sets jogs her memory, letting her piece together the mystery of her own fiery end.
"Within blood is life. Within life is fire. Within fire is the path to our masters' glory!"
The horror lurched about like a puppet from a madman's nightmare, squeezing the life from its own kind.
"Avacyn's protection is everywhere. From the holy church to the sacred glade, all that we see is under her blessed watch."

"Size alone does not guarantee survival."
—Vorinclex, Voice of Hunger
"So many oppose us, but we are the reed that bends without breaking."
An explorer's reward is a view of tomorrow's possibilities.

"To those who can hear it, Gaea's battle song brings power as swift as sunlight and as enduring as the deep roots of the forest."
—Gamelen, Citanul elder

"Life's greatest lessons don't come from focus or concentration. They come from breathing and simply noticing."
—Seton, centaur druid
If a spriggan's eyes are larger than its stomach, it has ways to remedy the situation.

"Krosa the great. Krosa the enduring. Look to the forest, and it will share its bounty."
—Zyd, Kamahlite druid
When it snared a passing cockatrice, its own soul darkly doubled.
Even what is lost beyond recall returns when coaxed by a dryad's hand.
In nature, not a single bone or scrap of flesh goes to waste.

"I am the simplifier, the root that drags all artifice to earth."
—Seal inscription
The Orzhov clergy would never cross its path, but sending thrull couriers to do so is cheap and entertaining.

"Give me enough refuse and mana and I will summon an ooze that can engulf all of Ravnica."
—Cevraya, Golgari shaman

"The hermit dies. The outcast dies. The lone wolf dies. Only those who stick together survive this world."
—Uros, Pendelhaven elder
"Not all paths are found on the forest floor."
What doesn't grow, dies. And what dies grows the tarmogoyf.

"Always carry two spears."
—Mokgar, Kalonian hunter
"Peace will come to Innistrad, but only after all abominations have been dealt with, one by one."

"For every one that falls, ten shall rise. The revelation of New Phyrexia is at hand."
—Vorinclex, Voice of Hunger
The Izzet quickly suspended their policy of lifetime guarantees.
The consciousness of Mat'Selesnya does not always spread in peaceful ways.
"Two-faced" is an understatement.
Life's circle has become inverted in Grixis. The same energy is endlessly recycled and becomes more stagnant with each pass.

"Finally, a weapon the Boros can't confiscate!"
—Juri, proprietor of the Juri Revue
They fight for their home with more loyalty than any conscript.
Frozen in fear, the goblins stared upward at the circling hunter—and were promptly eaten by its diving mate.
Centaurs are sent to evangelize in Gruul territories where words of war speak louder than prayers of peace.
Not the foulest or bloodiest act at Rix Maadi by a stretch.
Instructors at the Kasarna training grounds are capable healers in case their students fail to grasp the subtleties of combat.
Snaking remnants of nature directed by a body of thought and progress, the oracles embody all that is Simic.
There is always a greater power.
"Everyone deserves a day in court."

"Welcome to the Dimir Public Offices. Not responsible for death or loss of property. Basement off-limits."
—Sign outside Dinrova Building
You can always tell the evil one by the dagger he's sticking in you.
"Your blood is quite pleasing. A pity there's not enough for both of us."
When the rebels couldn't breach the castle to kill Lalor the Obstinate, they tried a more internal approach to depose the pretender king.

"The Simic come from the cold slow depths. How could they understand the fire in a wild heart?"
—Kroshkar, Gruul shaman
When asked how much power is required, Izzet mages always answer "more."
The Golgari don't bury their dead. They plant them.
Like corpse-worms through a carapace, rotwurms slide through the hollowed bones of the undercity.

"Taking down a dragon is easy. All you need is enough space to get in a good swing."
—Narbulg Nine Fingers

"We are the heart of the wild, the fire in its eyes, and the howl in its throat. Come, join the battle to which you were born."
—Kroshkar, Gruul shaman

"Touched by moroii"
—Undercity slang meaning "to grow old"

"The Simic can grow anything out of a puddle of sludge. I just hope they never join forces with the Golgari."
—Teysa Karlov, Grand Envoy of Orzhov
He has no patience for minds that do not inspire him or explode by trying.
Mirko Vosk hunted anyone with knowledge of the maze, draining the chances of the other guilds.

"We are all decaying, always in a state of near-death. One moment without breath and we begin to break down."
—Cevraya, Golgari shaman

Rhox monks are dedicated to spiritual growth and learning, and most bear the sigils of many students. However, they do not gladly suffer fools or those who disagree with their carefully wrought dogma.

"We've bred out the shortcomings of the species' natural form and replaced them with assets of our own design."
—Momir Vig
"That must weigh heavily on your soul. Let me purge it for you."

"I do not know which gives me more pride: the legions of soldiers marching in thunderous lockstep, or the cry of the skyknights riding their rocs like jagged lightning overhead."
—Razia

"Birth and death are both reversible."
—Nicol Bolas
"Let the knowledge of absolute law inspire you to live a life of absolute order."
For the Rakdos, "suicidal charge" and "good showmanship" are one and the same.
The vast network of predation on Jund has actually caused some strange creatures to adapt to being eaten.
Even the most battle-hardened soldiers pause in her presence for a moment of introspection.
"The volcanic winds make a maze of the skies of Jund. If we mean to invade, we must first learn their invisible paths."
All suns must set.

"Hear that? Those notes mean we've arrived at Sunhome! Let our allies' hearts soar and our enemies' hearts shatter at the sound!"
—Klattic, Boros legionnaire

"Esper, like any work of art, can be truly appreciated only from a distance."
—Tezzeret
As Trostani's influence grew, vitality spread through the Conclave—much to the other guilds' dismay.
As the Simic released more of their krasis experiments, they required new habitats, always at the expense of the locals.
Out of sight, into mind.
It provides what every discerning mage requires—time to think.
One of the most ferocious and deadly gargantuans, the thoctar never sees its worshippers, but it often awakens surrounded by gifts and sacrifices.
Zur remained aloof from Terisiare's suffering, intent only on his own perfection.

"Imagine a thunderstorm that's also a tactical genius. That's him."
—Dars Gostok, Firefist captain
Those who regard the Gruul as savage simpletons underestimate the subtle power of their shamans.

"Remember by whose gift you ascend."
—Milana, Orzhov prelate
Olka collected the evening mist for years, studying its secrets. Once she learned its essence, she could vanish with a thought.

"One day every pillar will be a tree and every hall a glade."
—Trostani
The Tattermunge gang has no words for the spell that whips their instinctual rage into a frenzy. They only know they like it.
The maze-like design embodies the core of Azorius law—strict structure designed to test wills and stall change.
During their endless travels, the mages of the Goma Fada caravan have learned ways to harness both life and death.

"Have you ever held a Boros signet? There's a weight to it that belies its size—a weight of strength and of pride."
—Agrus Kos
The priests tried cursing it. The mages tried dispelling it. In the end, they all obeyed it.
An emblem of a secret guild, the Dimir insignia is seen only by its own members—and the doomed.
Depending on your point of view, the seal represents a proud guardian of the natural cycle or one who has sold her soul to darkness for eternal life.

"If you wind up in one of mine, you can be sure as silver it will be your last."
—Grafdigger Wulmer
Gruul territorial markings need not be legible. The blood, snot, and muck used to smear them are unmistakably Gruul.
The Izzet signet is redesigned often, each time becoming closer to a vanity portrait of Niv-Mizzet.
The form of the sigil is just as important as the sigil itself. If it's carried on a medallion, its bearer is a master. If it's tattooed on the body, its bearer is a slave.
Made of bone and boiled in blood, a Rakdos signet is not considered finished until it has been used as a murder weapon.
The symbol of the Conclave is one of unity, with tree supporting sun and sun feeding tree.

For the Simic Combine, its sigil serves not as an emblem of honor but as a trademark. Its familiar image on any biological commodity attests to superb craftsmanship, ingenious innovation, and higher cost.

"We must rely on our own knowledge, not on the dogma of the seekers or the mutterings of the sphinxes."
—Tullus of Palandius
The Azorius symbol stares down like a great eye, reminding visitors of the watchful presence of Isperia and her lawmages.
It promises protection to those in need and proclaims a warning to any who would threaten Ravnican law.

"They say the ruins of Sedraxis were once a shining capital in Vithia. Now it is a blight, a place to be avoided by the living."
—Olcot, Rider of Joffik
In the cold corridors of the undercity, misinformation unfurls from Duskmantle like a spreading stain.
Every part of the gate was reclaimed from forgotten ruins and imbued with new purpose by the Swarm.
The scarred rubble around the gate is testament to past meetings of the Clans, summits that inevitably devolved into brawls.
Beyond lies the culmination of all Izzet projects, a grand experiment led by the dragon Niv-Mizzet himself.
On Naya, ambition and treachery are scarce, hunted nearly to extinction by the awe owed to terrestrial gods.

"We do not believe in hiding our wealth in the shadows. This is Orzhov, and this is how we reward greatness."
—Teysa Karlov, Grand Envoy of Orzhov
Maze-runners who pass through the Rakdos gate leave behind their scruples and a significant amount of skin.
Jund is a world as cruel as those who call it home. Their brutal struggles scar the land even as it carves them in its image, a vicious circle spiraling out of control.
For wisdom's sake, it was built high to gaze on all things. For glory's sake, it was built high as a testament of power. For strength's sake, it was built high to repel all attacks.
The Selesnya welcome all to help them heal the city's wounds. The price, however, is devotion to the guild and a selfless belief in Trostani.
Untold riches await those who forsake the bustling world to search the secret, silent places.
Simic biomancers don't concern themselves with guarding a gate. Their ever-present creations are enough to ward off trespassers.
She doesn't escort the dead to the afterlife, but instead raises them to fight and die again.
The people of Amrou were scattered by war and driven into hiding. Scouts maintain the beacon fires that signal "return" and "home."
The paradise of Amrou Haven had become a field of cinders. Its people struggled to survive, hoping to see visions of its past in the strange storms that quickly passed.
"Memnarch or the vedalken salvage most of the large machines, leaving us only scraps. Scraps are enough."
Today it flies with the flock. Tomorrow it may wake to find them gone, its body in an unfamiliar form.
A fight put off forever is already won.
The more the scarier.
Mages of Esper measure their wealth and status by the number of servants in their retinues.

"I find its symmetry pleasing. It rids our world of offensive refuse while disposing of itself."
—Dolomarus, Proctor of the Clean
"The noble work of our order is to infuse all life on Esper with etherium. Our goal will be reached more rapidly if new life is . . . suppressed."

"There are all kinds of strengths, but if you have strength of soul, the others will follow."
—Galanda Feudkiller
Its wings disturb more than air.
The giants believe the fossils they find in Lorwyn's rocky heights are dreams frozen in time, and they treasure them.

"Before the war, we prayed to Kataki to sharpen our swords and harden our armor. Without his blessing our weapons are all but useless against the kami hordes."
—Kenzo the Hardhearted
Sometimes a curious giant singles out a "little one" to follow for a few days, never realizing the effect it will have on the little one's life.

"The landscape shimmered and I felt a chill breeze. When my vision cleared, I found myself alone among the corpses of my fallen friends."
—Journal found in Numai
He remembers a past of light and healing. But he lives the bitter present—parching salt, scouring wind, and the withering heat of the desert.
As their supplies of etherium dwindled, mechanists sent gargoyles farther and farther afield in search of salvage.
It drifts through the streets as a breeze of collective sighs, wilting the bustle with dreams and heavy eyelids.
"No matter how strong, an unarmed fighter is no more than a fool."

"The jeweler, the potter, the smith . . . They all imbue a bit of their souls into their creations. The kami destroy that crafted mortal shell and absorb the soul within."
—Noboru, master kitemaker
Those who survive the test bear a mark of power anyone can recognize.
"Give me a sword and I'll kill a few enemies. But give me a hammer and a fiery forge, and I'll turn the tide of battle."

"Sages who take the time to verify their sources are rewarded for their diligence."
—Jhoira, to Teferi
A single lie unleashes a tide of disbelief.
The more metal it digests, the more its jelly will fetch on the alchemists' market.
The greatest masters of the craft abandon tools altogether, shaping metal with hand and mind alone.
Each spell is an intricate tapestry, and Kira is the great unraveler.
He loved his cities in the clouds. When he traveled to the lands below, he brought many reminders of his home.

"Ever seen a changeling fly into a lantern?"
—Calydd, kithkin farmer
It was created by the Iquati as a living memory—one that objects to being forgotten.
Those who expect betrayal at every turn are seldom disappointed.
When the School of the Unseen fell, so many magical treasures lay abandoned that no amount of death could deter the stream of thieves and desperate scholars.
The fae know when they're not wanted. That's precisely why they show up.

"Know one part of the name, obsession begins. Know two parts, paranoia sets in. Know three parts, madness descends. Know all, and only the kami know what will become of you."
—Lady Azami
Every culture has its unlucky numbers. In a city where you're either alone, in a crowd, or being stabbed in the back, two is the worst number of all.
"To truly know something, you must become it. The trick is to not lose yourself in the process."

"I crept up on him, quiet as a guttermouse. And then suddenly I found myself facedown in a latrine pit behind Tin Street Market."
—Sirislav, Dimir spy
One croaked sermon spreads propaganda and plague.
Greatness, at any cost.
The swarm's million wings stir the foulest of breezes.
Takenuma was filled with a chorus of moans, shrieks, and wails. Some came from the living, some from the dying, and some, most horribly, from the dead.
The barbarians of Jund believe the bottomless tar pits extend forever into other, darker worlds.
At night, the faeries steal dreamstuff for their queen. At daybreak, countless creatures wake weak and hollow.
There is always a moment of trepidation before opening a message capsule, for fear of the judgment that might be contained within.
Boggarts get so excited when they find something new to smash that they really don't notice who gets underfoot.
The line between dream and death is gauzy and fragile. She leads those too near it from one side to the other.
In life, it was a fetid, disease-ridden thing. In death, not much changed.
The fall of the evening star never heralds a gentle dawn.
One part cunning, one part wise, and many, many parts demented.
Like being trapped in a perpetual sneeze, faerie-dust poisoning is both exhilarating and agonizing.
Tangling vines, fetid murk, paralyzing poisons, and crawling dead. The swamp is nature's trap waiting to be exploited by unnatural minds.
It plucks away memories like choice bits of carrion.
Death is only the beginning of the end.
The lamps on Wyndmoor Street snuff themselves at midnight and refuse to relight, afraid to illuminate what lies in the darkness.
Leeches never tire of feeding.
"What do they need all this stuff for? They're dead. We're alive. Simple enough."

"And that's when it was discovered that boggarts have just half a brain."
—*The Book of Other Folk*
Among the solitude-loving giantkind, teamwork is unusual. But he appreciates hearing the occasional "Swing down and to your left."
Heavy light flooded across the landscape, cloaking everything in deep crimson.
Blood, bone, and sinew are magnified, as is the rage that drives them. The brain, however, remains unchanged—a little bean, swinging by a strand in a cavernous, raving head.

Five-toed grave
—Kithkin phrase meaning "a giant's footprint"

"They'd pour out of the warrens to make war (and to make room for the littering matrons)."
—*Sarpadian Empires, vol. IV*
Jund feasts on the unprepared.
Mages often seek to emulate the powerful relics lost to time and apocalypse.

"Take care what you offer the ignus. Food, perhaps. Coins. But nothing flammable!"
—Stovic, village eccentric
Some kami attacks during the war were rife with trickery, subterfuge, and subtlety, draining hope and pride from the mortal world. Other attacks were a lot more straightforward.

"It's difficult to heal a rift after it begins wandering about on its own."
—Teferi
From trinket to trauma.

"Some goblins are expendable. Some are impossible to get rid of. But he's both—at the same time!"
—Starke
Boggarts constantly strive to outdo each other with the things they bring back to the warren, each hoping the exploit will become as well-known as those of Auntie Grub.
Arc mages aren't known for their patience.

"Auntie Grub had caught a goat, a bleating doe that still squirmed in her arms. At the same time, her warren decided to share with her a sensory greeting of hot tar . . . ."
—A tale of Auntie Grub
He cares not for the disasters his storm brings as long as his path ahead is clear.
The giant was felt a few seconds before he was seen.

"Fire is the universal language."
—Jhoira, master artificer

"Aren't there boggarts enough in Lorwyn? Couldn't it turn into a sheep? Or a sunflower?"
—Olly of Goldmeadow
They seek out living trees to glean age-old secrets from sap and wood.
A single seed unleashes a flurry of growth.
She remembers every word spoken, from the hero's oath to the baby's cry.
Man's best fungus.
It grew in lands lit by pride and watered by tears.

"An ancient, powerful force has overtaken the valley. I sympathize for its former inhabitants, but I rejoice for the land itself."
—Olanti, Muraganda druid

"Tie a mouse under a bridge, and your cabbages will triple in size."
—Kithkin superstition

"The land grows only where the kami will it."
—Dosan the Falling Leaf

"Give up these unnatural weapons, these scrolls. Heart and mind and fist are enough."
—Zyd, Kamahlite druid
"Beauty determines value, and we determine beauty."
When it snared a passing cockatrice, its own soul darkly doubled.
Growth has no limits.
"Beings of the rifts are not natural. No longer will these abominations tread upon the body of Gaea."
Some who scouted new lands chose to stay.
What doesn't grow, dies. And what dies grows the tarmogoyf.
Ground into the footprints of the ravaging herd were clumps of salt from Benalia, moss from Llanowar, dust from Hurloon, and ash from as far as Urborg.
The Izzet learn something from every lesson they teach.
The Arbiter is a conduit of justice, a will so disciplined that it dispenses justice without ego or remorse.

"Knowledge of Bant's landscape and ruins is a weapon that the invaders can't comprehend."
—Elspeth

"Rage is not the answer. Rage followed by fitting vengeance is the answer."
—Ajani
During the collision of the shards, entire ways of life disappeared without a trace.

"The soul is only as eternal as I say it is."
—Sharuum the Hegemon
The Soul of the World has returned.
Held aloft by metabolized magic, trygons are ravenous for sources of mystic fuel.
She follows the old tributaries built when merrows still shaped the tides.

"His laugh, a bellowing, deathly din, slices through the heavens, making them bleed."
—*The Seer's Parables*

"She spoke of mystery and portent, of such unfathomable things that my mind screamed for pity."
—*The Seer's Parables*
Accept one favor from an ouphe, and you're doomed to accept another.

"Master the chaotic forces of nature, and you shall master magic."
—Yare-Tiva, warden of Gramur forest

"It was vast, a great sheet of soaring wings, and equally silent. It caught us unawares and blocked our view of the kithkin stronghold."
—Grensch, merrow cutthroat

"Release that which was never caged."
—Spellbomb inscription
The parts are as strong as the whole.

"It puts an end to what ails you."
—Jeorg, Valla battlemaster
At first, vedalken observers thought blinkmoths naturally avoided certain places. Then they realized those places were frogmite feeding grounds.
Most myr monitor other species. Some myr monitor other myr.
Mephidross gives up treasure easily . . . as long as you take its place.

"It contains the wisdom of generations of our people. We permit only a chosen few to don the raiment."
—Imran, Viridian elder

"Melt that which was never frozen."
—Spellbomb inscription
Elves believe the hydra-god Progenitus sleeps beneath Naya, feeding on forgotten magics.
When a changeling adopts a form no other changeling has taken, a rune appears in the caverns of Velis Vel to mark the event.
As the dawns break, the manta soars.
Its secrets once wrought the greatest artifice ever known. Now crabs loot the rubble to decorate their shells.

"There is much to learn here, but few can endure the ringing of the spires."
—Nulakam the Archivist
An empty canvas holds infinite possibilities.
Take two steps north into the unsettled future, south into the unquiet past, east into the present day, or west into the great unknown.

faces.f: Its mortar is mixed with waters straight from the Fountain of Cho.

We all must profit for peace to last.
—Mercadian saying
Orim had no memory of the previous night—the first thing she could remember was waking up with the dead guard's blood on her hands.
The perfect antidote for a tightly packed formation.
Are you sure you can afford such a luxury?
He doesn't know why the Cho-Arrim fight the Mercadians, but he's happy to bash heads for them anyway.

"Mercadia's masks can no longer hide the truth. Our day has come at last."
—Cho-Manno
Mercadia City's troops are at their best when they have no enemy to fight.

Don't step on the livelihood of other vendors, or they may step on you.
—Mercadian saying

"There is no place for mercy in defense of our lives."
—Ta-Spon, Cho-Arrim executioner
The crossbow is the ideal weapon for the lazy Mercadians: just point and shoot.
The Cho-Arrim fought Mercadia's decadence with more than just swords.

The scepter of power is fragile in a calloused hand.
—Cho-Arrim saying
The Cho-Arrim didn't rely only on a secret location to protect their Fountain.
Every Cho-Arrim villager is a potential warrior; when they are called, they abandon their peaceful way of life and take up arms to defend it.

"May the River claim Cho-Manno's body, wherever it lies."
—Ta-Karnst, Cho-Arrim healer
Cowardice is a term invented by those with no cunning.
A soldier's faith is magic strong enough to protect against any blade.
"I did not choose my role, Orim," said Cho-Manno patiently, "and I suspect Gerrard did not choose his."
War-trained jhovalls eat twice their weight in war-trained soldiers daily.
Don't be fooled by the riders' fluid grace—it takes years of practice to ride these beasts.
"The River flows. My soul returns."
The silence commemorates not those who've died, but those about to.

"As long as Rushwood glows, no life is ever truly lost."
—Ta-Karnst, Cho-Arrim healer

Clenched teeth do not bite.
—Cho-Arrim saying
Once you learn to float on the shadows, you'll never fear them again.
Fighting for the right reason is itself a source of strength.
The Cho-Arrim make no distinction between healers and soldiers.
The Cho-Arrim believe in leading by example.
"Cho-Manno guides your spirit. I guide your sword."
"Give me your hand and I will give you victory."
Her commands are part rallying cry, part sermon, and wholly undeniable.
The Cho-Arrim fell from the sky onto Mercadia City like a vengeful rain.
Gerrard offered no defense to Orim's condemnation; the mission was under his command, and he was responsible.
The Cho-Arrim worship life and revere those who've experienced it longest.

"There is a great difference between pain and injury."
—Cho-Manno
"You are the disease that plagues Mercadia. I am the healer's knife that will cut you out."
Orim taught Ta-Karnst and the other Cho-Arrim healers a far less invasive method of healing.
The Mercadians were prepared for the guard, but the guard was even more prepared for the Mercadians.
They are the reflection of Rushwood's glow on the edge of a wooden sword.

"The Mercadians are too busy looking down on us to see us coming."
—Cho-Arrim rebel
"The price is written at the bottom of the cup."
"How could I catch her when the trees conspired to stop me?"
Inner conflict can defeat a soldier more quickly than any army.
"It's not what you ask for, but how you ask for it."
Successful delivery is *not* guaranteed.
The market festival turned out to be the high point of Jaffy's visit.
"I need to get back to Mercadia City," said Sisay. "We can get you there," the vizier answered. "Easily."

"I see more than others do because I know where to look."
—Saprazzan vizier
In Mercadia City, loyalties extend only as far as your purse can stretch.
Saprazzan merfolk become legged on land, but some find it quicker to bring the water with them.
What's merely a home for the nautilus can become exquisite jewelry in the hands of Saprazzan artisans.
It was Gerrard's nature to lead and the Mercadians' to follow.
The delicate sprites carry messages for Saprazzans, but they refuse to land in Mercadia City's filthy markets.
"I don't like to think of myself as a pirate. I'm more like a stimulator of the local economy."

"Your attack has been rendered harmless. It is, however, quite pretty."
—Saprazzan vizier
Gerrard was the Mercadian soldiers' greatest hero; they followed him blindly. When he left, they stumbled around blindly.
A bribe is always faster than filling out paperwork.
You might as well try to catch water with a net.

"You say Saprazzo is a city built on water? I hope they have enough to wash the dust from my throat."
—Sisay
There is beauty in the space between learning to fly and taking it for granted.
Karn said nothing—he just grasped the powerstone and squeezed tightly. The wild flashing ceased.
The fewer your possessions, the fewer your worries.
"Go down there and fish him out. Maybe his hide will fetch a price."
Beautiful to behold, terrible to be held.
Don't trust your secrets to the sea.

Bend as the wave breaks or it will break you as well.
—Saprazzan saying
The youths of Rishada's marketplace are always ready for a quick footrace.

"I was there when Phyrexia doomed Serra's realm with a single touch. I was there when Yawgmoth tried and failed to conquer Dominaria. And I will still be here when Elesh Norn lies dead."
The weight of Phyrexia crashed down upon Gobakhan, but the will of its people endured.
When the sun falters and the seas disperse, when the wilds wither and the forges go cold, when death itself succumbs, she endures.
"Brother, guide my right hand. Sister, my left. Rest well, my kin, but Lorwyn still needs me. I will not be joining you quite yet."
Raised in a long tradition of heroes, every Benalish knight knows the day might come when they will be called to face Phyrexia.
An ancient weapon for a modern war.
"One path. Many feet."
Quintorius muffled a sob as he watched the thing that was once Professor Pitnik "confiscate" yet another priceless historical tome.
The Invasion Tree wasn't merely a conduit through which to breach planes. It was a living, writhing extension of Phyrexia's will.
Bim lashed out with the only weapon she'd never run out of: lecture notes.

n: Seraph of New Capenna // Seraph of New Phyrexia

faces.f: The angels had vowed to protect New Capenna. She was determined to uphold that vow, no matter the cost.
With her Halo reserves exhausted, she began to change, and she made a new promise to bless New Capenna with glistening perfection.
"Alara has been broken before. I will not let it break again."
Light glinted off the raised weapons of the Sun Empire, filling her with an unbreakable hope . . .
. . . but even the unbreakable can be reshaped.

"Let the light scour away your imperfect flesh."
—Heliod
No Meletian had ever laid eyes on an angel, but when protective Halo flooded the Multiverse, they knew a divine blessing was at hand.
The Royal Knights of Belenon are equally practiced in courtesy and combat.

"Obey the teachings of the dragonlords, for they provide all. They grant us magic and safety, and in return we offer respect."
—Baihir, Dromoka mage

"Your precious dragonlords repressed your instincts, cur. You were born a hunter. Evolve, and hunt again."
—Benzir, archdruid of Temple Might
The Phyrexians armored themselves against blades, fire, and every conjuration they could think of. She brought a war rhino.
Errant wouldn't allow anything to stop her from decorating the streets of New Capenna.
"You have no viable escape vector. Cease your resistance and accept perfection."
Izzet researchers agreed to keep the unusual weird contained until they understood the extent of its powers.
The Furnace Host saw no need for such caution.
"It's not your fault. Strixhaven taught you an imperfect premise. Okay, the imperfect execution was your fault."
Skills honed on perilous treasure hunts helped Zendikar's adventurers stay a crucial step ahead of their Phyrexian foes.
No longer bound by the myopic limitations of flesh, Ekken would truly see the realms.
Yuta Takahashi, World Champion XXVII
Where had she first seen that symbol? She usually took such detailed notes, but her memory of it was like a fading nightmare.
Innistrad's stitchers were practiced at incorporating magical substances into undead creations.

n: Invasion of Arcavios // Invocation of the Founders

faces.f: No professors, no grades, no room for mistakes.
The pace of Kamigawa's development meant that Jin-Gitaxias's intel was already outdated when the invaders arrived.

n: Invasion of Segovia // Caetus, Sea Tyrant of Segovia

faces.f:
"On my signal, disable the safeguards. Let's blow these metal freaks right back to their own world!"
—Gav Beleren, mage-ring engineer

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter.)
I — Draw cards equal to the number of cards in your hand. You have no maximum hand size for as long as you control this Saga.
II — Return all non-Phyrexian creatures to their owners' hands.
III — You may cast any number of spells from your hand without paying their mana costs. Exile this Saga, then return it to the battlefield (front face up).

faces.f:
"If something seems impossible, you probably haven't tried asking for help."
—Niambi, cleric of Dominaria
On the precipice of eternity, Elspeth made a choice. The fight would not end without her.
Teferi gave them time. Karn gave them a chance. But it was Melira who paid the ultimate price to free Ajani from Phyrexia's grasp.
Even before Phyrexia's forces arrived on Tarkir, Silumgar's draconic brood had a discerning eye for valuables.
After years of fabricating visions for naive customers of the Obscura, Stafano was flummoxed by the nightmarish scenes that played out unbidden in his mind's eye.

n: Order of the Mirror // Order of the Alabaster Host

faces.f: The Magic Mirror of Vantress showed Catrina a twisted vision of black oil and bloody machines.
Soon she understood that it was not the vision that had been twisted, but her own mind.
On Kylem, the omens of impending invasion went largely unnoticed, drowned out by the everyday fanfare of Valor's Reach.
"Ingress without proper writ of extraplanar intent? Unacceptable!"

n: Rona, Herald of Invasion // Rona, Tolarian Obliterator

faces.f: "At last, I am *compleat*."
"Good luck getting through a class-seven proxy ward, creep."
Together with her beloved falcon, she had explored every waterway on Zendikar, from the Tazeem highlands to the inland sea.
With her guidance, the oil coursed freely across the world.
Old glitches in mage-ring function became critical tools in Vryn's defense.
"Now's not a good time."
Just as all seemed lost, the griffin riders of Zhalfir arrived with the force of a gathered storm.
Wrenn reached out to Teferi through the Blind Eternities, and an impossible connection flared across the vast emptiness.
Phyrexia broke the laws of reality to invade the planes. On Xerex, reality merely bent around the invaders.
Patient and observant, the people of Zhalfir lurked beyond the veil of time until their moment came to finally strike at Phyrexia.
The Consulate of Kaladesh had always valued his particular talent for extracting information . . .
. . . but the Chrome Host's methods were far more efficient.

n: Ayara, Widow of the Realm // Ayara, Furnace Queen

faces.f: Ayara cherished her new machine servitors just as much as she once did her many suitors: not at all.
Mudcreep loved the taste of the funny oil that leaked from the wrecked machines in Urborg.
Then one day, Mudcreep started to feel funny itself.

"All worlds will know perfection."
—Elesh Norn
Night fell all at once. Specifically, on the Phyrexian.
The elves of Lorwyn sought perfection. The Etched Host supplied it.
Doji found the Phyrexian's essence foul, but every drop added an hour to their life.

"For the good of all, those who stand against the harmony of Phyrexia must be cut down."
—Ajani Goldmane
Daretti looked down disdainfully. "You call yourself machines? Where's the elegance? Nothing but ugly piles of scrap."
Bodies too damaged to survive phyresis are collected and broken down into useful raw materials.

"No refunds."
—Chammi, curio vendor
Strixhaven braced for another Oriq assault, but something far worse arrived.
As oil began to pour from Ikoria's crystals, some monsters developed strange mechanical mutations. Others were simply pulled under.
As oil seeped into their funeral shrouds, Tolvada's dead rose to join the invaders' ranks.
When the courts fell, Eldraine's fae turned from their usual pranks to deadlier tricks.

n: Invasion of Fiora // Marchesa, Resolute Monarch
Invasion of Innistrad // Deluge of the Dead

faces.f: The eerie magic animating Innistrad's zombies rendered them immune to phyresis, making them crucial to the plane's defense.

n: Invasion of Ulgrotha // Grandmother Ravi Sengir

faces.f: "I do enjoy a good apocalypse."
As the harvesters bore away the last of his limbs, what remained of Urabrask heard Elesh Norn say, "Leave the traitor be."
"You were my mistake. I will forever bear the weight of your horrors, and of your end."
Freedom became a distasteful memory, a thing to fear and destroy.
"Tell Boss Umezawa there's a new gang moving in on our territory. I'm forwarding their insignia. Watch for it elsewhere."

"Of course I'd rather it hadn't skinned six of my best wizards, but as nightmare fuel goes, it's a truly inspired design."
—Braids
As New Phyrexia phased out of existence, glistening oil all across the Multiverse was cut off from its source. The *compleated* invaders ceased to function and crumpled to the ground.
"Before I fall, I will taste the blood of Sarulf himself!"

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter.)
I — For each opponent, destroy up to one target creature or planeswalker that player controls.
II — Each opponent discards three cards, then mills three cards.
III — Put all creature cards from all graveyards onto the battlefield under your control. Exile this Saga, then return it to the battlefield (front face up).

faces.f: "My new form must be hard to understand."
On Amonkhet, Phyrexia found a ready-made army of horrors waiting for a new master.
When Atraxa first arrived, the people of New Capenna rejoiced at the sight of such a grand angel. Then the slaughter began.
The Furnace Host found great value in the chaotic ingenuity of Kamigawa's akki and allowed willing converts to "experiment" however they saw fit.
Ixalan greeted Phyrexia with a defiant roar.
"I have a reckless idea," Koth offered. Chandra grinned and cracked her knuckles.

n: Etali, Primal Conqueror // Etali, Primal Sickness

faces.f: The contagion spreads and the Multiverse quakes.
"Hold nothing back, my friends. Tonight we feast in Starnheim!"
With barely a moment's warning, a one-giant avalanche crashed into Kaldheim's defenders.
As strange portals roared open across Theros, Lydus gathered his prototype and fled. He was so close to perfecting his design.
Soaring in Realmbreaker's embrace, he finally understood what perfection was.
The rest of the Gatewatch retreated. Chandra and Wrenn went in blazing.

n: Invasion of Kaldheim // Pyre of the World Tree

faces.f: The warriors of Kaldheim burned the soul of their world to keep it out of Phyrexia's hands.
The crystal landslide stirred over the shattered forms of the Machine Legion vanguard, and then it rose and rearranged itself into an avenging colossus.
Inspired by tales of the legendary hero Squee, many young Kyren goblins strove to emulate his magical skill and courage in the face of danger.

n: Invasion of Regatha // Disciples of the Inferno

faces.f:
"The Phyrexians are fools if they believe they can weather such a storm."
—Sarkhan Vol
He stood his ground in the Mirrored Depths, his roar of defiance echoed by a thousand crystalline reflections.

"Bolas's methods were crude and inefficient, taking generations to refine the population into a reliable source of combat units. Still, it offers us something of a head start."
—Jin-Gitaxias
Nahiri's rage shattered hedrons into deadly, burning ruin.
"Zendikar must be broken before it can be saved."
With the ways between worlds thrown open, the Chain Veil's foul magic seeped from a vault deep within Ravnica all the way to Shandalar's dormant masters.
It'd played the same prank a hundred times, never noticing the flame's slowly evolving pattern.
When it realized the symbol's true, glorious meaning, it began marking every surface on Innistrad with oil-soaked claws.
"Good thing maintenance never got around to decatalyzing the bithermic plasma displacement conduits!"
